relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a man with 3 ABCA1 variants: "DNA sequencing revealed 3 heterozygous variants in the ABCA1 gene".
method_note: Hand-extracted; script used only to assemble JSON. One first-hand patient (label 'patient'). Two previously published children (ref 5, Fredrickson) included because the Discussion gives features for both ('2 children ... who presented with enlarged orange tonsils..., hepatosplenomegaly, mild corneal opacification, and marked HDL deficiency'); their features use evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'. The next sentence ('Their lipid profiles were characterized by mild hypertriglyceridemia, decreased LDL-C levels...') may describe Tangier patients generally, so low LDL, low apoA-I and hypertriglyceridemia were left not reported for them. Father (CABG at 58, PCI at 72) and brother (PCI at 54) are mentioned only as family history of coronary disease, not as ABCA1-tested or Tangier-affected, so they got no rows. Contradictions: the frameshift variant is called 'likely pathogenic nonsense mutation' in Investigation but '1 ABCA1 pathogenic mutation' in Discussion (pathogenicity recorded as 'likely pathogenic'; variant type recorded as 'frameshift' although the same sentence also says 'nonsense'). The two missense variants are called 'of uncertain significance' and later 'mutations causing amino acid substitutions'. The authors say the diagnosis is 'consistent with severe ABCA1 deficiency, but not Tangier disease' and elsewhere 'highly suggestive of Tangier disease but not definitive'. Variant phase undetermined ('chromosomal phase of the 3 variants could not be determined'), so zygosity is recorded as the stated 'heterozygous', not compound heterozygous. 'The liver and spleen size were normal' recorded as hepatomegaly and splenomegaly excluded (D-27). 'Did not have yellow or orange discoloration of his tonsils' does not exclude the composite checklist item 'orange-colored or enlarged tonsils' (enlargement not addressed). Corneal arcus counted as observed for checklist 'corneal opacity' (uncertain mapping). Coronary calcified plaque / 'progression of coronary atherosclerosis' counted as coronary artery disease observed although asymptomatic. Lipid values on lipid-lowering treatment (Table 1) were not used to mark low LDL or hypertriglyceridemia. Age 37 is the age at referral for low HDL-C, not a stated onset or diagnosis age, so onset left not reported. Vital status left not reported (only implied by 'continues to take'). 'His medical history was otherwise unremarkable' excludes nothing specific.
